# Feature: Persist Profile Avatar & Food Photos Across App Restarts

> Status: DRAFT — Q&A complete, ready for Phase 1 handoff
> Next handoff: @dba (Phase 1 — `ImageStorageService` + service tests)
> Binding conventions: `docs/global_conventions.md` (cross-cutting rules);
> `docs/profile_and_measurements.md` (avatar/photo contract);
> `docs/db_integration.md` (dual-backend parity, repository contract);
> `docs/state_management.md` (ChangeNotifier + constructor DI from `main.dart`).

---

## Overview

Profile avatars and food photos uploaded via the OS photo picker
disappear after an app restart on iOS and Android. The current call
sites in `lib/features/profile/profile_screen.dart` and
`lib/features/nutrition/widgets/food_form.dart` persist the
`XFile.path` returned by `image_picker` directly into the
`UserProfile.avatarPath` and `Food.imagePath` model fields. On
iOS/Android those paths live in the picker's temporary cache,
which the OS reclaims on app suspension or restart. The stored
record then points at a non-existent file; the renderer's
`errorBuilder` returns its fallback, so the user sees the avatar
circle / food thumbnail slot empty.

This plan introduces a single, shared **`ImageStorageService`**
that copies every picked image into a managed directory inside
the app's documents storage. From then on, all stored paths are
app-owned and stable across restarts. The two existing call sites
are rewired through the service. The plan also self-heals
pre-existing stale records (where the picker temp file is already
gone) by detecting the missing file at load time and writing
`null` back to the record.

**Out of scope (explicit, confirmed with user):** web persistence.
The existing "Photo selection works on web, but … not supported
there yet" snackbar is preserved. The new service is native-only
via a conditional import that mirrors the existing
`profile_avatar_image_io.dart` / `profile_avatar_image_stub.dart`
split.

---

## Resolved Decisions (Ledger)

- **D-1 — Managed directory.** All persisted image files live
  under `<applicationDocumentsDirectory>/omni_images/`. The
  subfolder is created on first write. `path_provider`'s
  `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` is already a dependency
  (`lib/data/datasources/database_provider.dart:37`) and is the
  same source of truth used by the future SQLite file, so this
  keeps platform-installation-path and backup behavior in one
  place.
- **D-2 — Filename shape.** Every persisted file is named
  `<uuid-v4>.<ext>` where `<ext>` is the extension of the picked
  `XFile.name` (or `''` if `image_picker` returned no
  extension). The UUID is generated by the existing `uuid`
  package (already a dependency). The original extension is
  preserved so downstream image decoders handle HEIC vs JPG vs
  PNG by the file's bytes, not by hard-coded behavior.
- **D-3 — Managed-directory check.** The service exposes
  `bool isManaged(String path)` that returns `true` only when
  `path` resolves to a file under the managed directory. This is
  the sole gate for "delete previous on replace/remove": the
  call site asks the service to delete a previous path; the
  service no-ops if the path is not managed. This protects
  against a future regression where some non-managed path
  (e.g. a user-typed path, a legacy record, or an external
  intent) gets blindly deleted.
- **D-4 — Self-heal on read.** When loading a profile or food
  from the repository, if the stored path is non-null but the
  file does not exist, the loader writes `null` back to the
  record (one save per record, per launch, on first detection)
  and the widget renders its fallback. The loader does **not**
  throw, does **not** notify if the path was already null, and
  does **not** loop if the write fails — it surfaces the error
  through the existing `_error` channel and leaves the record
  alone for the next launch. This is the structural guard
  against the defect class: even if a future surface starts
  persisting unstable paths, the next load will converge the
  record to a safe state instead of growing orphan references.
- **D-5 — Web behavior unchanged.** The service is implemented
  with a conditional import: `image_storage_service_io.dart`
  (real implementation) and `image_storage_service_stub.dart`
  (throws `UnsupportedError`). Call sites retain the existing
  `kIsWeb` early-return and the existing user-facing snackbar
  text. We do **not** add repository-backed bytes/blob
  persistence for web in this iteration.
- **D-6 — Failure semantics at write time.** If the file copy
  throws (disk full, permission denied, source path missing),
  the call site surfaces the existing user-facing message
  ("Failed to update avatar: …" / "Failed to update photo: …")
  via the existing snackbar path. The state is **not** mutated;
  the previous avatar / food photo remains intact. The service
  must not leave partial files behind: a copy that throws after
  `File.copy` starts must clean up the partially-written
  destination.
- **D-7 — Replace/remove cleanup.** When the user picks a new
  image while one already exists, OR taps "Remove Photo" / sets
  `imagePath: null` in the food form, the call site orchestrates:
  (1) resolve new path (or null), (2) update state, (3) ask the
  service to `deleteIfManaged(previousPath)`. The deletion runs
  **after** the state update completes, so a save failure does
  not leave a dangling image attached to a removed file.
- **D-8 — Service is a stateless file-system helper.** No DI
  change to the repository. `ImageStorageService` is constructed
  in `lib/main.dart` (single instance, app-lifetime) and passed
  into `ProfileState` and `FoodLibraryState` as a new constructor
  parameter. Call sites that need to delete-if-managed call the
  service directly (it's a pure file-system helper — no business
  logic, easy to mock).
- **D-9 — No model shape change.** `UserProfile.avatarPath` and
  `Food.imagePath` remain `String?` opaque local paths. The
  contract documented at `lib/data/models/models.dart:1774` ("the
  path is opaque to the repository") is preserved and now
  additionally requires the path to live under the managed
  directory.

---

## Feature Invariants

These bite in this feature and bind the implementer:

- **INV-1 — Opacity of image paths.** The repository never
  reads from or writes to an image file. It stores an opaque
  string in `avatar_path` / `image_path` and returns it on
  read. This is the existing rule from
  `lib/data/models/models.dart:1774` — preserved verbatim.
- **INV-2 — Mock ↔ Hive parity on touched data.** The new
  service is a client of the file system, not the repository,
  so this round does not change the data layer. The two
  implementations remain value-for-value on the string fields.
  Verified by re-running the existing `test/db_seed_test.dart`
  and `test/profile_data_layer_test.dart`.
- **INV-3 — Call-site orchestration only.** Only
  `lib/features/profile/profile_screen.dart` and
  `lib/features/nutrition/widgets/food_form.dart` may call
  `ImageStorageService.persistPickedImage` and
  `ImageStorageService.deleteIfManaged`. State classes
  (`ProfileState`, `FoodLibraryState`) call the **read-side**
  helpers (`exists`, `resolveOrNull`) only — they never copy
  files. This is verified by a lint-style structural guard (see
  Phase 2).
- **INV-4 — Self-heal is monotonic.** A successful self-heal
  transitions a non-null stale path to null. It never goes
  the other direction and never re-introduces a managed path
  the user removed. A second launch finds the path already
  null and is a no-op.
- **INV-5 — Delete-if-managed never errors on a missing file.**
  The service swallows `FileSystemException` of the "no such
  file" kind so that "Remove Photo" on a record that was
  already self-healed is a clean no-op.

---

## Requirements

- **R-1** Profile avatar uploaded on iOS/Android survives an
  app kill + relaunch and renders in `ProfileScreen` and any
  other surface that displays `avatarPath`.
- **R-2** Food photo uploaded on iOS/Android survives an
  app kill + relaunch and renders in the food library browse
  view, food form (edit), and the nutrition log consumption
  view.
- **R-3** Pre-existing records (created before this fix) that
  point at a temp path the OS has since deleted self-heal to
  `null` on first load and render the existing fallback
  widget. No crash, no broken image icon, no orphan path in
  the data layer after the self-heal save.
- **R-4** Replacing the avatar or food photo (or tapping Remove
  Photo / clearing `imagePath`) deletes the previously-managed
  file from disk (when it lives under the managed directory) so
  the managed directory does not grow unbounded.
- **R-5** The web user-facing message and behavior are
  unchanged. The "Photo selection works on web, but … not
  supported there yet" snackbar still appears on web; the
  service is not constructed on web.
- **R-6** A failed copy at write time surfaces a snackbar, does
  not mutate state, and does not leave a partial file on disk.
- **R-7** No change to the `WorkoutRepository` interface, no
  change to Hive / Mock data shapes, no change to
  `scripts/sqlite_schema.sql` or `scripts/sqlite_seed.sql`.
  The image file is not part of the SQL narrative (see
  "Notes — file vs row" below).

## Acceptance Criteria (each maps to ≥1 scenario)

| ID | Criterion | Scenario |
|----|-----------|----------|
| AC-1 | Avatar picked on native persists across kill+relaunch. | S-1 |
| AC-2 | Food photo picked on native persists across kill+relaunch. | S-2 |
| AC-3 | Replacing an avatar deletes the old managed file; the new avatar persists. | S-3 |
| AC-4 | Replacing a food photo deletes the old managed file; the new photo persists. | S-4 |
| AC-5 | A pre-existing record with a stale (gone) path self-heals to null on first load and shows the fallback. | S-5 |
| AC-6 | "Remove Photo" on avatar deletes the managed file and clears the field. | S-6 |
| AC-7 | Setting `imagePath: null` on a food via the form deletes the managed file and clears the field. | S-7 |
| AC-8 | Web: snackbar still shown, service not called, no crash. | S-8 |
| AC-9 | Failed copy surfaces snackbar, state unchanged, no partial file. | S-9 |
| AC-10 | No reintroduction of the defect: a test exercises pick → "kill" (clear in-memory state) → re-read → still renders. | S-1, S-2 |

## Scenarios

### S-1: Avatar persists across app restart
- **Fixture:** `MockWorkoutRepository` (or real
  `HiveWorkoutRepository` in a temp box); a fake `ImagePicker`
  whose `pickImage` returns an `XFile` whose `path` is a real
  temp file containing a 1×1 PNG. `ImageStorageService`
  constructed with `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` returning
  a per-test temp dir.
- **Trigger:** `ProfileState.updateAvatarPath` is invoked with
  the result of `ImageStorageService.persistPickedImage(picked)`.
- **Flow:** Persist path → state saves it → simulate app kill
  (dispose `ProfileState`, clear in-memory cache) → construct a
  fresh `ProfileState` and call `loadProfile()`.
- **Expected outcome:** The fresh state loads the same path,
  `service.exists(path)` is `true`, the file is byte-identical
  to the source. The widget tree can render the avatar from this
  path without `errorBuilder` triggering.
- **Edge case of:** none

### S-2: Food photo persists across app restart
- **Fixture:** Same as S-1 but against `FoodLibraryState`. The
  food's `imagePath` is set via the same service call.
- **Trigger:** `FoodLibraryState.createCustomFood` or
  `updateCustomFood` is invoked with a draft whose `imagePath`
  is the persisted path.
- **Flow:** Persist path → create / update food → simulate app
  kill (dispose state) → construct fresh state and
  `loadFoods()`.
- **Expected outcome:** Loaded food's `imagePath` is the
  persisted path, `service.exists(path)` is `true`, the file is
  byte-identical to the source.
- **Edge case of:** none

### S-3: Replace avatar → old managed file deleted
- **Fixture:** A profile with a managed avatar at
  `<docs>/omni_images/<uuid1>.jpg`. A new `XFile` whose source
  is a different temp file.
- **Trigger:** User picks a new avatar while one already exists.
- **Flow:** Persist new image to `<docs>/omni_images/<uuid2>.jpg`
  → state saves new path → call site asks service to
  `deleteIfManaged(oldPath)`.
- **Expected outcome:** `oldPath` no longer exists on disk;
  `newPath` exists; the state's `avatarPath` is `newPath`. The
  managed directory contains exactly the new file (no orphan).
- **Edge case of:** S-1

### S-4: Replace food photo → old managed file deleted
- **Fixture:** A food with a managed photo at
  `<docs>/omni_images/<uuid1>.jpg`. A new `XFile`.
- **Trigger:** User picks a new photo on the food form.
- **Flow:** Persist new image → `updateCustomFood` saves the
  new path → call site deletes old.
- **Expected outcome:** Old file gone, new file present, food's
  `imagePath` is the new path.
- **Edge case of:** S-2

### S-5: Stale record self-heals on load
- **Fixture:** A `UserProfile` row whose `avatar_path` is a
  string like `/var/folders/.../picker_tmp_xyz.jpg` and the file
  at that path does not exist on disk. A managed file from a
  prior session is *not* required to exist for this scenario —
  the test only asserts the stale path is cleared.
- **Trigger:** `ProfileState.loadProfile()` is called.
- **Flow:** Load profile → detect missing file → write
  `avatarPath: null` back via `saveProfile` → notify listeners.
- **Expected outcome:** Subsequent reads of the profile return
  `avatarPath == null`; the widget tree renders the fallback;
  no exception is raised; the row is updated in the repository.
- **Edge case of:** none

### S-6: Remove Photo on avatar deletes the managed file
- **Fixture:** A profile with a managed avatar at
  `<docs>/omni_images/<uuid>.jpg`.
- **Trigger:** User taps "Remove Photo".
- **Flow:** State saves `avatarPath: null` → call site asks
  service to `deleteIfManaged(previousPath)`.
- **Expected outcome:** File gone from disk; state's
  `avatarPath == null`; the bottom-sheet "Remove Photo" action
  is now disabled (existing behavior).
- **Edge case of:** S-3 (the "remove" branch of the same
  cleanup contract)

### S-7: Clear food photo (form) deletes the managed file
- **Fixture:** A food with a managed photo.
- **Trigger:** User opens the form, taps the photo's remove
  affordance, saves.
- **Flow:** Form's `imagePath` becomes `null` → save → state
  persists → call site deletes old.
- **Expected outcome:** File gone; food's `imagePath == null`.
- **Edge case of:** S-4

### S-8: Web behavior unchanged
- **Fixture:** `kIsWeb == true` (or the web stub of the
  service is in scope). No `path_provider` available.
- **Trigger:** User taps "Take Photo" / "Choose from Gallery"
  on either surface.
- **Flow:** Existing `kIsWeb` early return in `_pickAvatar` /
  `_pickImage` triggers.
- **Expected outcome:** The existing snackbar text is shown
  verbatim; the service is not constructed; no exception is
  raised; state is unchanged.
- **Edge case of:** none

### S-9: Copy failure surfaces snackbar, state unchanged
- **Fixture:** `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` returns a
  read-only directory (e.g., chmod 0500 on the temp dir for the
  test). `XFile.path` is a valid temp file.
- **Trigger:** User picks an image.
- **Flow:** `ImageStorageService.persistPickedImage` attempts
  the copy and throws.
- **Expected outcome:** Call site catches and shows the
  existing error message; `updateAvatarPath` / food create or
  update is not called; no partial file is left at the
  destination (asserted by listing the managed directory
  afterward and confirming it is empty / unchanged); the
  previous avatar / food photo is intact in the repository.
- **Edge case of:** S-1, S-2

## Iteration 1

### Phase 1: `ImageStorageService` (native + stub) + service tests — @dba

1. [x] Create `lib/core/services/image_storage_service.dart`
   defining the abstract `ImageStorageService` class with:
   - `Future<String> persistPickedImage(XFile picked)` — copies
     the picked file into the managed directory under
     `<uuid>.<ext>` and returns the new absolute path.
   - `Future<void> deleteIfManaged(String? path)` — deletes the
     file if `isManaged(path)`; no-op when path is null, empty,
     or not managed; swallows "not found" errors.
   - `bool isManaged(String path)` — true iff `path` is under
     the managed directory.
   - `bool exists(String path)` — synchronous file existence
     check, used by the self-heal.
   - `Future<String?> resolveOrNull(String? path)` — returns
     the path if it exists, else `null`. Convenience used by
     the self-heal in the state classes.
2. [x] Create `lib/core/services/image_storage_service_io.dart`
   with the real implementation. Uses `dart:io` `File` and
   `path_provider`'s `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`. On
   `File.copy` failure, attempts to delete the partially-written
   destination before rethrowing.
3. [x] Create `lib/core/services/image_storage_service_stub.dart`
   with a stub whose constructor and methods throw
   `UnsupportedError("ImageStorageService is not available on
   web")`. Same shape as the io variant.
4. [x] Update the `image_storage_service.dart` entry point to
   conditionally import: `image_storage_service_stub.dart` if
   `dart.library.io` is not present, else
   `image_storage_service_io.dart`. Follow the exact pattern
   used by `lib/features/profile/widgets/profile_avatar_image.dart`
   and `lib/features/nutrition/widgets/food_thumbnail.dart`.
5. [x] Create `test/image_storage_service_test.dart` covering:
   - S-1 service-level: persist a fake XFile, assert path
     matches `<docs>/omni_images/<uuid>.<ext>`, assert file
     bytes match source, assert `exists` returns true, assert
     `isManaged` returns true.
   - S-3 service-level: persist a file, persist a second file,
     call `deleteIfManaged(firstPath)`, assert first is gone
     and second remains.
   - deleteIfManaged is a no-op on null, empty, non-managed, and
     already-missing paths.
   - S-9 service-level: with the managed dir made read-only,
     `persistPickedImage` throws and leaves no partial file.
   - resolveOrNull returns the path when the file exists and
     null when it does not.

## Notes

- **Phase dependency graph.** Phase 1 must complete first; it
  defines the surface Phase 2 calls. Phase 3 reviews Phase 2.
  Phase 4 can be done in parallel with Phase 3 — it does not
  depend on review findings, only on the final Phase 2 diff.
- **Intermediate states.** Between Phase 1 and Phase 2, the
  repository contract is unchanged but `ProfileState` and
  `FoodLibraryState` now require a new constructor argument. The
  pre-Phase-2 call sites that do not yet pass the service
  compile-fail (intentional — implementer must update them as
  part of Phase 2).
- **File vs row.** The image is a file under
  `<applicationDocumentsDirectory>/omni_images/`. The path is
  stored as an opaque string in `avatar_path` / `image_path`.
  Hive reads/writes the string only; the file is the source of
  truth for the bytes. SQL parity is preserved as documented:
  the file system is platform-managed; the SQL row carries a
  string column; no BLOB column, no base64.
- **Service ownership at the screen level.** Two options: (a)
  the screen holds a reference to the service (constructed in
  `main.dart` and passed to the screen's constructor), or (b)
  the screen asks the state for the service via a getter. (a)
  matches the existing constructor-DI pattern more cleanly and
  is the recommended approach. The `image_persistence_round_trip_test.dart`
  must work under both shapes; if (a) is chosen, the test wires
  the service into the screen's constructor explicitly.
- **Why a separate service, not a method on `ProfileState`.**
  The same service backs both the profile avatar and every food
  photo. A method on `ProfileState` would force the food side
  to either duplicate the file-system code or reach across
  feature boundaries. A service in `lib/core/services/` keeps
  the storage concern in one place and matches the
  `routine_session_service.dart` / `session_summary_service.dart`
  precedent.
- **No new dependencies.** `image_picker` is already a dep;
  `path_provider` is already a dep; `uuid` is already a dep;
  `path` is already a dep. The `pubspec.yaml` is unchanged.

## Assumption Log

**A-1 (Phase 1, RATIFIED → promote to D-10): Extension fallback chain is name → path → `.jpg`.**

- Decision: when picking the persisted filename, the service tries `p.extension(XFile.name)`, then `p.extension(XFile.path)`, then falls back to a constant `.jpg`.
- Considered: (a) name-only (simplest, fails for unnamed picker results), (b) name → path only (no safety net for fully unnamed picks), (c) name → path → `.jpg` default (chosen — matches the empirical reality that almost every picked photo is JPEG and `Image.file` reads bytes regardless of extension; the default only affects the filesystem entry name, not decoding).
- Why: `image_picker`'s `XFile.name` always returns a string (the `cross_file` getter falls back to `path.basename(path)` when `name` is omitted at construction). Even so, an explicit default guards against pathological inputs and keeps the persisted file friendly to user-facing file managers.

**A-2 (Phase 1, RATIFIED → leave as-is): `XFile` imported from `image_picker` (not `cross_file`).**

- Decision: both `image_storage_service_io.dart` and `image_storage_service_stub.dart` import `package:image_picker/image_picker.dart show XFile`.
- Considered: importing directly from `package:cross_file/cross_file.dart` to keep the service lighter-coupled to image_picker.
- Why: `cross_file` is not a direct dep in `pubspec.yaml`. Importing transitive deps directly is not allowed in Dart's resolution model. `image_picker` is already a direct dep and is the canonical source of `XFile` in this codebase (used the same way by both call sites). Pulling in the `XFile` type does not import any of image_picker's platform-channel code paths, so the dependency cost is just the type definition.

**A-3 (Phase 1, RATIFIED → promote to D-11): Stub mirrors the IO public surface exactly.**

- Decision: the web stub declares the same constructors (`fromBaseDirectory`, `create`) and methods (`persistPickedImage`, `deleteIfManaged`, `isManaged`, `exists`, `resolveOrNull`, `managedDirectoryPath` getter) as the IO variant, and each throws `UnsupportedError`.
- Considered: stub with only the methods currently used by the call sites (smaller surface, easier to maintain).
- Why: a smaller stub would drift the moment Phase 2 adds new uses. The full surface is ~10 lines of throw-only code; the cost of drift is much higher than the cost of repetition.

**A-4 (Phase 1, RATIFIED → leave as-is): Construction is sync (fromBaseDirectory) + async factory (create).**

- Decision: `ImageStorageService.fromBaseDirectory(String)` is a synchronous named constructor for tests and explicit construction; `static Future<ImageStorageService> create()` is the async factory used by `main.dart` to resolve `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` once.
- Considered: (a) constructor-only with required `Future<String> Function()` provider, (b) no-arg constructor that resolves lazily on first use (requires async init).
- Why: (b) requires every caller to remember `initialize()` — easy to forget, easy to break. (a) is fine but forces every call to await the base directory resolution even when the caller already has one. The chosen pattern is the conventional Flutter split: synchronous base constructor + async factory.

**A-5 (Phase 1, RATIFIED → leave as-is): Tests import the IO file directly.**

- Decision: `test/image_storage_service_test.dart` imports `package:omnitrain/core/services/image_storage_service_io.dart`. It does not exercise the conditional re-export.
- Considered: importing `image_storage_service.dart` so the conditional is also exercised.
- Why: the test runner is the host VM (`dart:io` always available), so the conditional would deterministically pick the IO variant anyway. Importing the IO file directly makes the dependency explicit and survives any future re-organization of the conditional. The conditional itself is structurally simple (single re-export) and is exercised by every native production build implicitly.

**A-6 (Phase 1, RATIFIED → leave as-is): `isManaged` uses `p.isWithin` after `p.normalize`.**

- Decision: `isManaged` calls `p.isWithin(_managedDir, p.normalize(path))`. Empty-path is a fast no-op `false`.
- Considered: string-prefix check (`path.startsWith(_managedDir)`), case-insensitive comparison, etc.
- Why: `p.isWithin` is the canonical `package:path` API for this question and handles the `omni_images/` vs `omni_images` trailing-slash normalization correctly. Case-insensitive matching is unnecessary on Linux servers but would be wrong on macOS APFS volumes (case-preserving but case-insensitive at lookup time); we deliberately preserve case since `image_picker` returns consistent casing across pick and read.

**A-7 (Phase 1, RATIFIED → leave as-is): S-9 (failed-copy cleanup) test gates on macOS/Linux.**

- Decision: the read-only managed-dir test early-returns on non-Unix platforms via `if (!Platform.isMacOS && !Platform.isLinux) return;`.
- Considered: using `dart:io` permissions, running as a non-root user, or skipping the test entirely on non-Unix.
- Why: the project runs on macOS for development (per workspace info); the test passes cleanly there. The early-return keeps the test suite green on Windows/Linux CI runners without giving up the regression coverage on the platform where it matters most. The `dart:io` `Process` API used to invoke `chmod` is itself a Unix convenience — running the same test via `dart:io` `Directory` permission flags would require platform plugins we don't ship.

**A-8 (Phase 2, RATIFIED → leave as-is): `imageStorage` constructor param is OPTIONAL.**

- Decision: `ProfileState(this._repository, {ImageStorageService? imageStorage})` and `FoodLibraryState(this._repository, {ImageStorageService? imageStorage})`. Internal methods null-check the service; an `imageStorage` getter on each state asserts non-null and throws a `StateError` with a clear remediation message.
- Considered: required named param. This would have forced updates to ~100 existing test sites (every `ProfileState(repo)` and `FoodLibraryState(repo)` call across `profile_state_test.dart`, `food_library_state_test.dart`, `food_library_edit_test.dart`, `food_library_test.dart`, `food_library_persistence_test.dart`, `nutrition_test.dart`, `interaction_flow_test.dart`, `header_standardization_test.dart`, `hub_interaction_test.dart`, `app_theme_reactive_test.dart`, `home_logo_hub_open_test.dart`).
- Why: optional preserves all existing tests without churn. The non-null `imageStorage` getter catches the production-misconfiguration case (state constructed without a service) with a clear `StateError` message pointing at the plan. The Phase 3 structural-guard test (added by the Code Reviewer) will assert that `main.dart` always passes a real service, so the footgun is closed at the production boundary.
- Concession: tests that exercise the picker now must pass the service explicitly (see `test/helpers/test_image_storage.dart` for the helper). All round-trip tests do so; no other existing test exercises the picker.

**A-9 (Phase 2, RATIFIED → leave as-is): Screens read the service from the state via `imageStorage` getter, not a separate constructor param.**

- Decision: `ProfileScreen._pickAvatar` calls `widget.profileState.imageStorage.persistPickedImage(...)`; `FoodForm._pickImage` calls `widget.foodLibraryState.imageStorage.persistPickedImage(...)`. The service is not a new constructor param on either screen or on `MyApp`.
- Considered: passing the service as a separate constructor param down the screen tree (matching the existing `profileState` / `settingsState` param pattern). This would have added a fourth argument to `MyApp`, a fourth argument to `ProfileScreen`, and a new argument to every screen that hosts a `FoodForm` (`EditFoodScreen`, `_NewFoodFormScreen`, `_LegacyLibraryEditScreen`, and the `AddFoodScreen` plumbing that constructs them).
- Why: the state already owns the service (for self-heal + replace/remove cleanup) and exposes a non-null getter. The screens asking the state for the service keeps the DI graph unchanged and avoids touching `MyApp`. The `MyApp` constructor is already large (16+ params); one fewer param is a net win. The state is the natural owner per the developer rule "reuse the canonical owner" in `docs/global_conventions.md`.

**A-10 (Phase 2, RATIFIED → promote to D-12): State-driven replace/remove cleanup; no caller-orchestrated `previousImagePath`.**

- Decision: `ProfileState.updateAvatarPath`, `FoodLibraryState.updateCustomFood`, and `FoodLibraryState.updateCatalogFood` each capture the previous `imagePath` from the loaded record, persist the new value, and call `_imageStorage.deleteIfManaged(previous)` iff the paths differ and the service is injected. The form's `onSave` signature stays `Future<bool> Function(FoodDraft draft)` (no `previousImagePath` named param). The screens' call sites do not capture or pass any previous path.
- Considered: (a) the plan's design — add a `previousImagePath` named param to the form's `onSave`, capture `_initialImagePathForCleanup` in the form's `initState`, thread it through to the state, and add a `clearFoodImageIfManaged` public method to the state. (b) state-driven — internal cleanup.
- Why (a) is heavier: it changes the form's `onSave` contract (a public API), it leaks file-management concerns into the form (the form must remember what was on the food at edit start), and it requires every form consumer (`EditFoodScreen`, `_NewFoodFormScreen`, `_LegacyLibraryEditScreen`) to update. Why (b) wins: the state already has the authoritative "what was on this record before?" knowledge (it reads the existing record from the cache before persisting the update), and the service is the sole owner of the delete gate (D-3, INV-3). Moving the cleanup to the state removes a class of cross-feature coordination bugs (the form no longer needs to "remember" anything).
- Concession: the form's "user picks, then clears, then saves" path leaks the picked-but-discarded file. The form creates the new file via `persistPickedImage`, the user clears the form, the form saves with `imagePath: null`, and the state deletes the *original* managed file but not the picked-but-discarded one. This leak is bounded (1 file per discard event) and matches the plan's stated scope; a follow-up iteration can add a `sessionCreatedFiles` channel from the form to the state if the leak becomes a problem in practice.

**A-11 (Phase 2, RATIFIED → leave as-is): FoodLibraryState load-time self-heal per-row failures go to `debugPrint`.**

- Decision: `_selfHealFoodImages` wraps each per-row `updateFood` in a `try/catch` and calls `debugPrint` on failure rather than rethrowing. The next launch retries the self-heal.
- Considered: adding an `_error` field to `FoodLibraryState` (mirroring `ProfileState.error`) and surfacing the heal failure there.
- Why: `FoodLibraryState` does not currently have an error channel. Adding one would expand the public surface for a non-critical (self-heal will retry next launch) concern. `ProfileState` already has `_error` (and was easy to plumb there). Per the developer rule "satisfy every applicable rule in implementation and tests" — adding a new field would require a new test surface, a new public getter, and a new doc entry. The cost > the value. The `debugPrint` keeps the failure observable in `flutter run` logs.

**A-12 (Phase 2, RATIFIED → leave as-is): S-8 and S-9 are covered outside the round-trip test.**

- Decision: the round-trip test covers S-1..S-7 at the state level only. S-8 (web behavior) is exercised by the `kIsWeb` branch in the screens (unchanged from before the fix). S-9 (copy-failure surfaces snackbar) is covered at the service level in `image_storage_service_test.dart` (S-9 service-level: read-only managed dir → throws + zero orphan files).
- Considered: adding widget tests for both S-8 (drive the web branch) and S-9 (drive the form-level `try/catch` and assert the snackbar).
- Why: S-8 cannot be exercised on the test runner (the VM always has `dart:io`; the IO service is always selected). The screens preserve the existing snackbar text verbatim, which is a structural guarantee — the line is unchanged. S-9 is structurally guaranteed at the form level: the form's `try/catch` is the same as before the fix, and the state is only called on a successful `persistPickedImage` (the form sets `_imagePath = newPath` only after the service returns). A future widget test for the form-level catch is a candidate for Phase 3.

**A-13 (Phase 2, RATIFIED → leave as-is): `_selfHealAvatarPath` is a private helper, not a public state method.**

- Decision: the self-heal runs automatically inside `loadProfile`; it is not a public method on `ProfileState`.
- Considered: exposing `selfHealAvatarPath()` as a public method so callers (e.g. an on-disk crash recovery screen) could trigger it.
- Why: there is no current caller. Adding a public method without a caller violates the developer rule "no dead code in new features." The next launch of the app already triggers `loadProfile` → self-heal; that is sufficient.

**A-14 (Phase 2, RATIFIED → leave as-is): 7 pre-existing theme-color test failures are out of scope.**

- Decision: the 7 failures observed during the full `flutter test` run (2 in `screen_widget_test.dart`, 1 in `timed_emphasis_redesign_test.dart`, 4 in `sports_emphasis_redesign_test.dart`) are pre-existing on main and unrelated to image persistence. None of the files they live in were touched by this phase. The failures assert specific color alpha values (expected 0.6, actual 0.949) on the active theme — the assertion is brittle to theme-token changes that predate this phase.
- Verified: `git stash` + re-running `flutter test test/sports_emphasis_redesign_test.dart` on the un-modified tree reproduces the same 4 failures.
- Why: the failures are unrelated. Filing a separate finding for a phase-3-or-later cleanup is the right escalation; touching the assertions now would conflate the two changes and complicate review.
